head_coach_candidates.name: Marcus Whitaker
head_coach_candidates.background: Built quick passing scripts that protect the quarterback early. Has not owned defensive staffing, so the defensive coordinator must control personnel, practice priorities, and late-game calls.
strengths: Red-zone calls that turn drives into points
Tempo packages that protect leads late
weaknesses: Defense must be assigned to the coordinator
Late-game clock choices have cost wins
head_coach_candidates.interview_quote: Give me a quarterback who processes fast, then assign defense and late-game calls before kickoff.

elias_vance.analysis: Whitaker gives the quarterback structure fast before Week 1. Before hiring him, assign the defensive coordinator to defensive personnel, practice priorities, and late-game calls; otherwise clock and defensive mistakes cost wins.
elias_vance.one_liner: Hire him for offense, then assign defense and late-game calls before those mistakes cost wins.

derrick_coleman.analysis: Whitaker gives the quarterback quick passing answers. His spread offense leaves defense and the run game underbuilt without a defensive coordinator owning personnel, practice priorities, and late-game calls.
derrick_coleman.one_liner: Assign defensive personnel and late-game calls before hiring him, or Week 1 run-defense jobs and coverage calls get exposed.

maya_alvarez.analysis: Marcus gives the quarterback and skill players quick passing structure. Without defensive coordinator ownership over personnel, practice priorities, and Week 1 calls, run-defense jobs and coverage calls are exposed.
maya_alvarez.one_liner: Assign defensive personnel, practice priorities, and Week 1 calls first; otherwise run-defense jobs and coverage calls get exposed.

head_coach_candidates.name: Victor Ramos
head_coach_candidates.background: Twenty-year defensive coordinator who demands exact practice roles and tackling work. Has never been a head coach, so offensive play-call authority must be settled before Week 1.
strengths: Coverage disguise that creates turnover chances
Linebacker roles tied to run, blitz, and coverage jobs
weaknesses: Power-run preference makes late drives predictable without play-call control
Offensive coordinator conflict slows Week 1 calls
head_coach_candidates.interview_quote: Give me tackling rules, third-down jobs, and one offensive play-caller before kickoff.

elias_vance.analysis: Ramos lowers defensive mistakes with contact and assignments. If the offensive coordinator lacks play-call and adjustment control, his power-run preference makes late drives predictable.
elias_vance.one_liner: Assign offense play-call control before hiring him; otherwise late drives get predictable.

derrick_coleman.analysis: Ramos reduces defensive mistakes with contact work, assigned roles, and third-down tackling. Keep offensive control with the playcaller or late drives get predictable.
derrick_coleman.one_liner: Hire Ramos for defense, then protect offensive control or late drives stall.

maya_alvarez.analysis: Victor teaches defense, but two former offensive coordinators described split staffs. Coordinator conflict slows offensive adjustments and creates different practice rules for offense and defense unless the offensive coordinator has final play-call authority.
maya_alvarez.one_liner: Pass until the offensive coordinator controls play calls; otherwise staff conflict slows Week 1 adjustments.

head_coach_candidates.name: Jamal Brooks
head_coach_candidates.background: Former Pro Bowl running back turned assistant head coach. Stabilized practice roles and accountability after a staff transition, but has never called plays.
head_coach_candidates.interview_quote: Give me assigned roles, a trusted playcaller, and a game manager, or morale cannot save fourth-down mistakes.

elias_vance.analysis: Brooks repairs player morale, but he has not owned play calls. That leaves fourth-down, timeout, and adjustment decisions in other hands by Week 1. Hire the playcaller first and keep Brooks in an assistant role.
elias_vance.one_liner: Pass for the top job; no play-call owner leaves Week 1 fourth-down and timeout mistakes exposed.

derrick_coleman.analysis: Brooks steadies sideline morale. Fourth down, timeouts, and coordinator accountability still need a proven game manager. Hire him with assigned playcallers who own fourth downs, timeouts, and coordinator fixes, or mistakes cost drives.
derrick_coleman.one_liner: Hire him with a game manager, or fourth-down and timeout mistakes cost drives.

maya_alvarez.analysis: Jamal calms players after a GM firing and improves free-agent recruiting. Unproven playcallers leave fourth-down calls and in-game adjustments behind by Week 1 unless proven playcallers are attached.
maya_alvarez.one_liner: Hire him with proven playcallers or fourth-down and timeout mistakes cost drives.

scouting_director_candidates.name: Calvin Hendricks
scouting_director_candidates.background: Thirty-four years scouting college players. Finds late-round talent through coach reports, practice habits, and repeated film reads; medical and athletic data must match the file before picks are spent.
scouting_director_candidates.philosophy: Judge effort, toughness, and practice habits, then match them with medical and athletic data before we spend picks.
strengths: College-coach reports tied to practice habits
weaknesses: No medical or athletic cross-check before picks wastes cheap picks on players who cannot practice
Slow data updates leave injury and testing warnings late before picks
scouting_director_candidates.interview_quote: Show me effort, practice notes, and medical limits before we spend a pick.

elias_vance.analysis: Cal has missed too many recent Day 3 starter roles. Audit injury tracking and athletic limits before hiring him; without medical data, cheap picks get spent on players who cannot practice or earn jobs.
elias_vance.one_liner: Pass until injury data clears him; otherwise cheap picks go to players who cannot practice or earn jobs.

derrick_coleman.analysis: Hendricks sees effort, toughness, and practice habits that the combine misses. The cost is slower data adoption, so pair him with medical and athletic data before picks are spent.
derrick_coleman.one_liner: Hire Cal with medical data; missing it wastes cheap picks on players who cannot practice or earn jobs.

maya_alvarez.analysis: Cal's college-coach reports reveal character and practice habits. Pair him with medical and athletic data before picks, or injury and athleticism warnings stay hidden.
maya_alvarez.one_liner: Pair Cal with medical and athletic data before early picks, or injury warnings get missed.

scouting_director_candidates.name: Priya Desai
scouting_director_candidates.background: Built a pick-cost warning system that found productive mid-round starters. Never scouted on the road full-time, so regional scouts must report toughness, coachability, and medical warnings.
scouting_director_candidates.philosophy: Turn data into draftable starter reports before other teams find the same role.
weaknesses: No road-scout report before early picks misses toughness, coachability, or medical warnings
No road-scout visit leaves coachability, effort, or character warnings hidden
scouting_director_candidates.interview_quote: If we cannot measure it, study tape and medical limits before we pay for it.

elias_vance.analysis: Priya turns scattered reports into role, medical, and cost warnings tied to picks. Limited road work means regional scouts must report toughness, coachability, and medical warnings before rounds two through four.
elias_vance.one_liner: Hire her, then pair reports with road scouts or mid-round misses cost picks.

derrick_coleman.analysis: Desai brings data reports, but the lead scout also needs coach, family, and practice input. If we hire her, assign veteran road scouts before picks are spent or toughness and effort misses cost picks.
derrick_coleman.one_liner: Assign road scouts before picks are spent, or toughness misses cost picks.

maya_alvarez.analysis: Priya brings data-backed reports and coachability notes. Limited road scouting misses how prospects respond to coaching, so pair her with a veteran evaluator before picks are spent.
maya_alvarez.one_liner: Pair her reports with a road scout before early picks, or missed coachability detail costs snaps.

scouting_director_candidates.name: Theo Washington
scouting_director_candidates.background: Started as area scout, became director of pro personnel, then college director. Known for making data staff and road scouts name each prospect's job, medical limit or coachability warning, and pick or cap cost before decisions.
scouting_director_candidates.philosophy: Combine data reports, coach input, and live evaluation before we spend picks or cap space.
strengths: Data and road-scout reports tied together
Coach communication before picks or signings
Pro free-agent roles named before spending
weaknesses: No specialist comparison leaves data and tape conflicts unresolved before picks
No coach-owned development plan passes over unusual prospects or wastes their snaps
scouting_director_candidates.interview_quote: Every report must name the player's job, medical limit or coachability warning, and pick or cap cost.

elias_vance.analysis: Theo lines up data and road scouting before picks. Coaches and scouts name the player job, medical limit or coachability warning, and pick cost before draft night. Unusual prospects get passed over when no coach owns their development plan.
elias_vance.one_liner: Choose Theo before picks are spent so reports name the player job, warning, and pick cost.

derrick_coleman.analysis: Washington makes scouts and coaches name the player job, medical limit or coachability warning, and cap or pick cost before a signing or draft pick. Unusual prospects get passed over when no coach owns their development plan.
derrick_coleman.one_liner: Choose Theo before contracts or picks lock so reports name player jobs and medical warnings.

maya_alvarez.analysis: Theo makes data staff, road scouts, and coaches file the same player job, warning, pick-cost, and cap-cost report. Unusual prospects get passed over when no coach owns the development plan.
maya_alvarez.one_liner: Hire Theo before picks or cap space are spent so medical and role warnings are named first.

what_is_a_head_coach.elias_vance: Your head coach is your chief decision-maker on game day, responsible for fourth-down calls, timeouts, challenges, practice priorities, and coordinator authority. Hire the coach who owns those calls before Week 1 mistakes become losses.
what_is_a_head_coach.derrick_coleman: The head coach sets practice roles, scheme rules, fourth-down calls, and who plays on fourth-and-one. Hire someone who makes hard calls without creating morale loss.
what_is_a_head_coach.maya_alvarez: A head coach sets practice roles, conflict rules, and game-day accountability. Pick someone with clear coordinator authority, or close games become blame, morale loss, and slow development.

what_is_a_scouting_director.elias_vance: The scouting director turns college reports into player roles, medical warnings, and pick-cost calls before draft day. A role-disciplined hire protects picks; a hire without role discipline costs picks, cap space, and development snaps.
what_is_a_scouting_director.derrick_coleman: The scouting director ties live film, practice habits, coach notes, and medical limits to pick decisions. That hire decides which reports name pick cost or cap-space cost before decisions.
what_is_a_scouting_director.maya_alvarez: Your scouting director puts scouts, coaches, and your roster plan on the same player job, warning, pick-cost, and cap-cost report before we spend picks. Name character warnings because a role mismatch costs development snaps, cap space, and later fixes.

why_scheme_matters.elias_vance: Scheme decides which players carry each snap. Match it to your quarterback, line, and coverage players or Week 1 mistakes multiply.
why_scheme_matters.derrick_coleman: Scheme tells players how they must win. Power run needs line play and backs who finish; Tampa 2 needs safeties who stay deep and corners who tackle. Pick calls that fit the blockers and coverage players you have by Week 1, or missed assignments start there.
why_scheme_matters.maya_alvarez: Set scheme calls that match your people, not the other way around. Name what the line protects and what the quarterback must decide quickly. If calls do not match the roster, players hesitate and Week 1 mistakes multiply.

what_is_the_salary_cap.elias_vance: The cap is the budget for keeping, replacing, and adding players. Pushing money into future years creates dead money, so tie each spend to a named starter, injury, trade, or extension need.
what_is_the_salary_cap.derrick_coleman: Spend cap space on players who still produce, your own starters, and injury fixes. Dead money on players who no longer play blocks injury replacements and extensions.
what_is_the_salary_cap.maya_alvarez: The cap limits who we keep, replace, or add. Extensions reward core players; cuts and restructures create morale loss and dead money. Before spending next-offseason cap space, name whether the move protects Week 1 depth, owner patience, and later injury fixes.

what_are_season_goals.elias_vance: Goals tell ownership what you are promising. A high win goal pushes trades and free agency harder; a development goal protects young snaps but makes early losses louder.
what_are_season_goals.derrick_coleman: Goals decide what ownership judges. Division title means faster veteran upgrades and fewer rookie mistakes tolerated. Development means young players keep snaps, but losses hit owner patience.
what_are_season_goals.maya_alvarez: Season goals tell players what ownership will judge. A win target moves trades and lineup choices into this week's decisions; a development goal protects young-player snaps but makes early losses louder. Pick the goal the roster must defend before October losses cut owner patience.

how_the_draft_works.elias_vance: The draft buys future starters with limited picks. Trade back when reports show no tier break, trade up only for a clear tier break, and avoid spending picks on players the staff cannot develop.
how_the_draft_works.derrick_coleman: Draft buys future starters with limited picks. Name effort, assigned role, medical limits, and practice habits before the pick; testing alone wastes cheap roster spots.
how_the_draft_works.maya_alvarez: How does the draft work for us? We are choosing who gets four years of development snaps and cap space. Interview for character, coachability, and assigned role because a talented miss still costs picks, time, and expensive veteran fixes.

elias_vance: Coach hire is set. Choose scheme and depth cover before Week 1 or the hire does not protect the starters he was hired to coach.
Set weekly prep around his assignments; without it, player mistakes rise by Week 1.
Hire staff who cover his assignment misses before scheme mistakes cost drives.
derrick_coleman: Coach hire is set. Match his scheme and depth chart to the roster before Week 1.
Set players and weekly prep to his scheme, or missed assignments cost games.
Set the depth chart now; missing backup order leaves his Week 1 roles unprotected.
maya_alvarez: Protect this coach with scheme and depth choices before Week 1; otherwise players enter the opener with unassigned calls.
Match scheme, depth chart, and weekly prep to his assigned roles before morale drops and assignments slip.
Name his role plan before kickoff; without it, Week 1 jobs stay unassigned.

elias_vance: Open scout reports before pick deadlines; fewer handoffs reduce missed starter and backup assignments.
Make this hire reduce middle-round misses before cheap roster spots get wasted.
Pair each data report with live scout notes before pick cost locks in.
derrick_coleman: Scout hire is set. Name film, effort, and medical limits in every report before picks are spent.
Match film notes to the first open role before draft weekend; otherwise picks buy players the staff cannot use.
Fix incomplete reports before draft weekend or cheap roster spots get wasted.
maya_alvarez: Set each report to role, character warning, and pick cost before pick decisions cost development snaps.
Attach role, character warning, and pick cost to every report before picks are spent.
Apply those named reports before draft picks cost development snaps on players the staff cannot develop.
